### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s).

**14** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via user_id (literal, a string literal in assertDirectGrantWrite))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via user_id (literal, a string literal in assertDirectGrantWrite))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via user_id (literal, a string literal in assertDirectGrantWrite))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via permission_set (literal, a string literal in directGrantSet))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx`  _(via user_id (literal, a string literal in assertDirectGrantWrite))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via user_id (literal, a string literal in assertDirectGrantWrite))_

- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via permission_set (literal, a string literal in directGrantSet), user_id (literal, a string literal in assertDirectGrantWrite))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via business_unit_id (literal, a string literal in assertAssignmentWrite))_
- `content/docs/permissions/positions.mdx`  _(via business_unit_id (literal, a string literal in assertAssignmentWrite), user_id (literal, a string literal in assertDirectGrantWrite))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via DelegatedAdminGate (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via business_unit_id (literal, a string literal in assertAssignmentWrite))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via user_id (literal, a string literal in assertDirectGrantWrite))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via permission_set (literal, a string literal in directGrantSet))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eca7cd2008c7aa5174b451428b8b73b29b237299` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c1b0c7fdefb12030d08200763af13fd60714577e` — the merge of head `da7d298fd20cf6053cd62936c1e2baa829452bac` into base `eca7cd2008c7aa5174b451428b8b73b29b237299`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c1b0c7fdefb12030d08200763af13fd60714577e && git checkout c1b0c7fdefb12030d08200763af13fd60714577e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eca7cd2008c7aa5174b451428b8b73b29b237299 da7d298fd20cf6053cd62936c1e2baa829452bac && git checkout -B drift-repro eca7cd2008c7aa5174b451428b8b73b29b237299 && git merge --no-ff da7d298fd20cf6053cd62936c1e2baa829452bac

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eca7cd2008c7aa5174b451428b8b73b29b237299
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eca7cd2008c7aa5174b451428b8b73b29b237299` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f29ee6a49d4089bc97d576d74440ef670a225ceb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, .changeset/assignment-write-unaddressable-row-not-found.md, .changeset/delegated-admin-unreadable-row.md, .changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/org-admin-assignment-boundary.posture.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/delegated-admin-assignment-write-unreadable-row.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/org-admin-assignment-removal-unreadable-row.dogfood.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-inputs.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-admission.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/grant-permission-set-name.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/organization-scope.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts, packages/core/src/utils/record-not-found.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/engine-update-dispatch.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/engine-delete-dispatch.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AssignedUsersSection.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PositionHoldersSection.tsx

Reviewed against rulings B and sub-item B (maintainer, 2026-11-04, batch 4 item 2) and the governing ruling of record 5985885287 on #21771; prior state is #29932 and #29950 (merged). Read-only: the diff from the merge base, the PR body, the check-runs on the head, and the cited code at the head. Nothing built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Rule 1 — a by-id assignment write the administrator cannot address answers the read door's not-found.** Holds, and holds as one producer.

- The not-found is built by `recordNotFoundError(object, id)` from `@objectstack/core`, which is the one producer the read door (`assertRecordExists`, `protocol-record-reads.ts`) and step 2.7 of the middleware already call, with the same two arguments. The middleware gives the id from `addressedByIdWriteId`, the same reader step 2.7 uses, so status, code, name, message and own fields cannot differ from step 2.7's for that object and id. The posture rig compares the whole answer against both the producer and the tenant-level administrator's step 2.7 answer under `group` and `isolated`; the two dogfood pins compare the whole HTTP response of `PATCH` and `DELETE` with a `GET` of the same id, for the row and for an id naming none.
- Every caller class the ruling names reaches it: the organization administrator without a scope (the organization branch's refusal is marked), the delegate and the organization administrator who also holds a scope (the organization branch's marked refusal is not thrown when scopes are held; the delegated walk then marks its own). `single` is covered for an id naming no row; a row another organization owns is readable there, so it keeps its guidance — correct, the ruling only equates what the caller cannot read with what is absent.
- A caller the read door refuses outright still gets that read refusal: the middleware re-asks the read before it looks at the marker, and the refusal wins. Unchanged from #29950 and pinned (`writeOnlyDelegate`).
- The three step-2.7 exclusions are the same function (`addressedByIdWriteId`: a nested write, the referential field clear, anything the engine does not route by id), so a nested write and a referential clear keep the gate's own refusal, which names no row and no id. The write-admission preview (`canWriteObject`) folds every `PermissionDeniedError` to `false`; the marked subclass extends it, so the preview answers the same boolean for a hidden row, a missing row and a readable row it may not write. Correct per step 2.7's own exclusions.
- Nothing is still split by row presence inside the ruling's two verbs: every earlier refusal of the gate (audience anchor, principal-less context, `sys_member`, no active organization, no scope, filter write) is taken before any row is read and answers the same whatever the id; every later one is taken after the read, which has already answered a hidden or absent row alike. The organization administrator's edit in place is now asked the read question first, so an edit of a readable row is still refused as an edit (403) and an edit of an unreadable one is the not-found; a reader who may not write keeps 403, as the ruling requires.
- The marked subclass is not on the public surface: `index.ts` re-exports `DelegatedAdminGate`, `isTenantAdmin` and the `DelegatedAdminGateDeps` type from the gate module and nothing else; the predicate is a module export the middleware imports directly and no published baseline names it.

**Rule 2 — a refusal names a stored value only when the caller can read it.** Holds for the delegated branch; the organization branch is addressed under ③ (2).

- "Can read" is the read door's own answer: `readAsCaller` is the operation's memoised `getCallerPreImage`, which is the engine's `findOne` under the caller's context, and that read passes through step 4 of the middleware, which deletes a column the caller's field map denies and replaces a partially masked one with its masked value before the result is returned. `columnsReadAsStored` then keeps only the columns the caller's read returned at strict equality with the system read, so a hidden column is absent and a masked one differs; neither is named. A read the door refused contributes no column. Sound: the dev's reason (a partially masked column stays in `getReadableFields`) is right, and the chosen comparison does not depend on that set at all.
- A masked or partially masked value cannot reach the sentence or `details`: the four columns a refusal could name (`position`, `business_unit_id`, `user_id`, `permission_set`) each go through `mayName`; the grant's column is `GRANT_SET_NAME_FIELD = 'permission_set'`, the column `mayName` is asked for, so the two readers agree. `details` carries `position` or `permissionSet` only under the same test; the containment sentence takes an unnamed form beside an unnamed position or set. A catalog fact (which set a position distributes) is named only beside a named position. A value the caller wrote (an insert's row, a column its update payload carries) is its own and is named; for a merged update, a column the payload does not carry falls through to the read test.
- The verdict is still the stored row's in the delegated branch: `prev` is the system read once the caller's read returned a row or was refused, as #29950 left it; only the wording changed. The posture rig pins each of the four columns hidden from the caller: same verdict, no hidden value anywhere in the serialized refusal, and the value named for the delegate who reads it.

**§6 (`security-findings.md`) on the title, body, changesets, commit messages and test names:** each states the hardening rule (what a write answers, what a refusal names), none describes a probe or an attack. Commit messages and test names carry the rule. Code comments cite the ruling record, which the rule-provenance convention allows; no runtime string carries a tracker number. No breach.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/plugin-security` at `patch`, `Clause-②: no` with no arm, `Metadata-protocol: none`, on the PR body and all three changesets. Correct.
- The dev's open question 3, answered from AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: "`Clause-②: yes|no` plus at most one arm from the closed pair `(widening)`/`(narrowing)` (`(narrowing)` is BREAKING, `no (widening)` malformed)", and the level gate's own reading of the line (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`): "`Clause-②` keeps its MEANING (does this diff widen or narrow a published accept set or public surface)". A 403 to 404 swap on refusals widens nothing and narrows nothing: every write admitted before is admitted, every write refused before is refused, and no export moves. So no arm, and `no` is right. The same reading carried #29950's 404 to 403 swap on `Clause-②: no`.
- `single` posture: an id naming no row now answers 404 where #29950 had it answer the gate's 403. Same test, same answer: a refusal's status, not the accept set; the declaration does not change.
- The two unreleased changesets: neither has shipped (`CHANGELOG.md` holds neither; the package is at 18.3.0). `check-empty-changeset` reds on both and its own text names this case as a DELIBERATE CORRECTION whose remedy is "do NOT restore it, say so on the PR and get it confirmed"; the PR does that. Each edit is right where it rewrites the first bullet. One should-fix on the second file: `.changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md` keeps "An edit in place is refused as before" under Unchanged, and an edit of a row the administrator cannot read is now the not-found; say "an edit in place of a row it reads is refused as before" (the new changeset already says this). Tier S landing waits on the maintainer's confirmation of both corrections and on every check green: at the time of this read, `Check Changeset` is red by design and Build Core, Type Check (workspace, consumer gates) and the Test Core shards were still in progress; every finished check is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **UI census, recommendation A (no UI change): accepted.** The two Setup removal surfaces (`AssignedUsersSection.tsx`, `PositionHoldersSection.tsx`) show the server's sentence from the error body or message and fall back to a localized line; neither branches on the status or the code, and a grep of `ui/` for the two codes beside assignment, position or holder handling finds nothing. The only visible change is the sentence a removal of a row removed in between now shows.
2. **The organization branch judges the caller's read; the delegated branch judges the stored row. Already decided by the ruling text, not a maintainer question.** Ruling B names both ADR-0090 D12 gate branches, and sub-item B's "The verdict stays on the stored row" carries no branch qualifier. The organization branch takes its verdict from the caller's own read (`organizationTargets`, from #29932), so a row inside the boundary whose judged column (`position`, `permission_set`, `organization_id`) a field rule hides from the administrator is refused ("the assignment names no position", "the grant names no permission set", "the row carries no organization") where the stored-row verdict would admit it. Fail-closed: no admission widens, no hidden value is named (the posture rig pins that), and the ruling's answer for an unreadable row is untouched. **Should-fix**, in this PR or an immediate follow-up: once the caller's read returns a row, take the organization branch's verdict from the stored row and its wording from `mayName`, as the delegated branch does. Not a FAIL: the deviation is prior state, fail-closed, and discloses nothing.
3. Covered in ②.

### ④ Design judgment

Tried to break the rule; no must-fix found.

- **Id from `where` instead of the payload.** The gate's `extractSingleId` and the engine's dispatch (`resolveEngineUpdateDispatch`, `resolveEngineDeleteDispatch`) both read the payload id first, then `where.id`; the rigs write with `where: { id }`. They part only on a falsy scalar payload id (`''`, `0`), which the engine does not count as an address but the gate does: the gate then reads that id, and the middleware answers for `where.id` (the not-found when that row is hidden or absent, the gate's refusal when it is readable). Hidden and absent still answer alike for every shape; a readable row may get a 403 for a degenerate input. Pre-existing; a note, not a finding. A `where` carrying more than the id with `multi: true` routes to the predicate path, where the middleware does not convert and the gate's refusal stands for a hidden and an absent id alike.
- **Refused for another reason on a row the caller cannot read.** Every refusal of the gate that depends on the row is taken after the read, so the read's answer comes first (no `manageAssignments`, subtree, allowlist, containment, unresolved set, no target user, no anchor). Every refusal that does not depend on the row is taken before the read and does not vary with the id. The self-delegation path is insert-only. No split by presence.
- **Bulk or multi write.** A delegate's write without one scalar id is refused before any read; an organization administrator's filter delete likewise, and its filter update is refused as an edit without a read. An array payload is read as a predicate. Nothing reads a row, so nothing can answer by presence.
- **Explain and admission.** `explainAccess` asks the gate only whether the caller covers the explained user (`organizationAdminCoversUser`, `scopesCoverUser`), never a write verdict. `canWriteObject` passes a synthetic operation with no `options`, so a delete preview is refused as a filter write before any read and an update preview reads by payload id; its answer is a boolean either way, so a hidden row, an absent row and a readable row the caller may not write answer the same `false`.
- **Lifecycle verbs** (`transfer`, `restore`, `purge`) stay outside the ruling's two verbs: the delegated walk marks its refusal and the middleware does not convert, so a hidden and an absent row both get the gate's 403 for a single caller. No presence split; noted, not a finding.
- **Should-fix (a pin):** the posture rig hides columns (`readable: false`); no case exercises a partially masked column, and the strict-equality reading is what keeps a masked value out of a refusal. One case with a masking rule on `position`, asserting the masked and the stored value are both absent from the refusal, would pin that rule where it lives.
- **Should-fix (text):** the changeset clause named under ②.

Findings: no must-fix. Should-fix: ③ (2) the organization branch's verdict on the stored row; ② the Unchanged clause of `.changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md`; ④ a pin for a partially masked column.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-r`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `da7d298fd20cf6053cd62936c1e2baa829452bac`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/org-admin-assignment-boundary.posture.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/field-masker.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-inputs.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts

Delta review by the same reviewer, on `git diff f29ee6a49d40..da7d298fd20c` only: one commit, two files (53 insertions, 4 deletions), no change to the middleware, the gate or the other two changesets. The PASS at `f29ee6a49d4089bc97d576d74440ef670a225ceb` (comment 6638950952) stands for everything outside this delta; its ① to ④ are not restated. The PR body was rewritten for this head and is read again below. Read-only: nothing built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **No change to the accept set or the public surface.** The delta touches a pending release note and a test file; the two rules the earlier record judged (an unaddressable assignment write answers the read door's not-found; a refusal names a stored value only when the caller can read it) are unchanged in code.
- **Should-fix ② of the earlier record, applied.** `.changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md` now reads "An edit in place of a row it reads is refused as before" under Unchanged, which is what the gate does at this head: an edit of a readable row is refused as an edit, an edit of a row the administrator cannot read is the not-found (named in the first bullet and in the new changeset). The sentence is true.
- **Should-fix ④ of the earlier record, applied.** The posture rig gains a partially masked column under `isolated`: a `maskingRule` (`keepHead: 3, keepTail: 0`) declared on `sys_user_position.position`, read by the plugin's own `field.maskingRule` reader (`security-plugin.ts`) and served to the delegate masked rather than deleted, as the rig first pins by reading the row as the delegate and comparing with `maskFieldValue`, the masker's own producer. For both verbs it asserts the refusal is `DELEGATION_SCOPE_VIOLATION` and that neither the masked value, nor the stored value, nor the set the stored position distributes appears anywhere in the serialized refusal; and, in the other direction, that a row whose stored position is inside the scope is admitted for both verbs although the delegate reads it masked. That is the rule where it lives: a column counts as read only at its stored value, and the verdict is the stored row's either way. The PR body's one-shot ablation A3 (presence counts as read) reds exactly this case, which measures that the strict-equality reading is load-bearing.
- **§6 (`security-findings.md`) on the rewritten body, the changeset edit, the commit message and the test name:** each states the hardening rule. The new Tests bullet and the A3 ablation line name a rig fixture and the pin's own failure, not a probe; the commit message carries the two rules; the test name carries the rule. No breach.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged: `@objectstack/plugin-security` at `patch`, `Clause-②: no` with no arm, `Metadata-protocol: none`, on the body and all three changesets. The delta publishes no code and moves no export.
- `Check Changeset` is red by design on this head too (the same two deliberate corrections, awaiting the maintainer's confirmation); a second run of it and of `PR-body guards` was in progress at the time of this read, after the body rewrite. Every other check on `da7d298fd2` is green: Build Core, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Test Core 1 to 8, the Lint families, the Governed Surface Queue Guard, the Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI and Live E2E UI. Tier S landing still waits on the maintainer's confirmation of the two corrections and on every check green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The earlier record's ③ (2), the organization branch taking its verdict from the caller's read where the ruling places it on the stored row, is unaddressed by the seat's choice and is to be a separate order. It was a should-fix, fail-closed, prior state from #29932; it does not change this verdict. The body's "It is pinned here and not changed" sentence about that branch is accurate.
- No new flag is raised by the delta; the body's open questions are the earlier ones, answered in comment 6638950952.

### ④ Design judgment

- The new case is one `it` in the existing describe, booted through the same harness with one variation (`boot(posture, { positionMaskingRule })`), so it runs against the same engine, driver and plugin as the rest of the rig; the masked precondition is asserted before the writes, so a green run cannot mean the rule never applied. The admitted leg deletes the in-scope row and reads the table back, so it also pins that the masked read does not turn an admission into a refusal.
- One note, not a finding: the case runs under `isolated` only. The masking rule and the strict-equality reading are posture-independent (the masker is step 4 of the middleware for every posture), and the hidden-column case already runs under all three postures, so one posture pins the rule.

Findings: no must-fix; no new should-fix. Two of the three earlier should-fix items are applied; the third is deferred to a separate order by the seat.

Red by design · head `da7d298fd20cf6053cd62936c1e2baa829452bac` · 2026-11-04T19:58Z

**Gate:** `Check Changeset` (`scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`).

**Cause:** this PR edits two pending changesets it did not create, `.changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md` and `.changeset/delegated-admin-unreadable-row.md`, which came from PRs #29932 and #29950. This change makes their "answers 403" sentence false. The gate classes that edit as a DELIBERATE CORRECTION and stays red until the correction is confirmed in writing on this PR, which its header calls "the existing human path". Both contract-review records find the edits right: comment 6638950952, and the delta record on this head.

**Why the red does not block anything else:** `pr-automation.yml` runs on `pull_request` only, never on `merge_group`, and this check is not a required context.

**Still owed:** the maintainer's written confirmation on this PR. The seat will not land the PR until it is posted.
